design_condition: Two offset volumes flank the boulevard, preserving generous open space in front and three planted open spaces toward the track field, while partly failing to connect directly to the viaduct side.

positive.statement: The very clear and controlled urban planning creates a well-sized and easy-to-read statement.
The access structure is clear, concise, flexible, and implemented in an exemplary manner.
The ground-floor uses are intelligently placed and support attractive connections with the outside space.
The project promises to be economical and sustainable because of its simple volumes.

negative.statement: Direct access from the viaduct side is missing, despite being easy to implement.
The space under the viaduct is undefined and insufficiently convincing, with required connections and parking provisions unresolved.
The access system becomes mechanical and repetitive because the upper-floor sequence lacks spatial weighting.
Many essential spatial relationships are not maintained, making the flow of people and goods and orientation more difficult.
The long internal paths and weak connection of the entrance hall to public uses require special functional attention.
The narrow inner courtyards provide only limited daylight to adjacent rooms.
The high proportion of glass is likely to have a negative impact on the energy balance.
